definition: Settings is the vault's one configuration manifest; there is only ever one, and its id is always default. Its first purpose is the purpose: the vision and mission every goal serves, stated once above the whole strategy (TAXONOMY.md D24; the balanced scorecard's mission and vision, Kaufman's ideal vision). The strategy reads top-down from it: the purpose, then goals, objectives and outcomes, and a gap is measured against it. A goal with no vision or mission above it cannot be judged Relevant. Its other fields are configuration: the vault's own words for the levels of the strategy and for a project, the author recorded when no one is signed in, the browser used to render documents, and examples in the vault's own words. Settings is not a goal (the purpose sits above the goals and has no measures of its own), not a programme or a project, and not a place for any one team's aims.

/metadata/id.guide: Always default: Settings is a singleton, and a save refuses any other id.

/spec/purpose.guide: The vision and mission, with where they are published. When they come from a published plan, quote them word for word and give the plan's section as the source.

/spec/purpose/vision.guide: The future the organisation is working towards, in one or two sentences: the state of the world it wants, not what it does. No figures: those belong to the goals' measures.
good: Every member can make a dependable living from what they grow.

poor.why: A target, not a vision: the figure and the date belong in a key result under a goal.
Says nothing a goal could be judged against: best at what, for whom?

poor.text: We collect, check and sell our members' produce.
poor.why: What the organisation does is the mission; the vision is the future it is working towards.

/spec/purpose/mission.guide: What the organisation does to get there, and for whom, in one or two sentences. It names the standing work, not a list of projects.
good: We collect, check and sell our members' produce together, so each member gets a fair and dependable price for a season's work.

poor.text: Roll out quality checks at every depot and open two new depots.
poor.why: A list of pieces of work that end, which are projects; the mission is what the organisation does all the time.
Values, not a mission: they do not say what the organisation does.

/spec/purpose/source.guide: Where the vision and mission are published, precisely enough to find again: the document, and the section or page. Leave it empty when they are written here first.

poor.why: Not precise enough to find again, and a page that changes is not a source.

/spec/goalLevels.guide: The names this vault shows for the three levels of the strategy, in order: goal, objective, outcome. Change them only to use the words of the organisation's own plan; the meaning of each level stays the same. Leave it empty to keep Goal, Objective and Outcome.

poor.why: Functional names part of an organisation, not a result; the third level is a changed state.
An output is what a project produces; the third level is an outcome, a changed state.

/spec/projectLevelName.guide: The word this vault shows for a project, when the organisation's plan uses its own, such as Initiative. A project is still work that ends.

poor.why: A programme is a different thing: it coordinates projects and operations towards one change.

/spec/operator.guide: The author recorded on a saved version when no one is signed in, such as a change made from the command line. It defaults to local. Name the deployment or the role that runs it, never a person.

poor.why: A person: Cartograph records people only as signed-in principals, never in a definition.

/spec/chromium.guide: The path to a Chromium browser used to render documents as PDF. Leave it empty to use the CHROMIUM environment variable, or the first Chromium on the path.

/spec/examples.guide: Examples this vault shows behind the question mark on a field, in its own people's words, keyed by field (such as aim.change, objective or gap.current), up to five each. A field without an entry shows the product's own generic examples.
good: aim.change: Every depot checks produce against one published standard.

poor.why: An example teaches by being copied, so it must be written as the discipline would: the figure belongs in a key result.

/metadata/name.guide: The title shown in lists, kept the same as the name: both are required, and they should never differ.
